messages:
maria: heads up — the python quickstart in /docs/quickstarts/python fails for newcomers if they copy-paste the env var name 😬

maria: example in the README shows `Redwood_API_KEY` but the SDK looks for `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (all-caps). confused a couple of interns today. error is just `AuthenticationError: missing api key`

devon: ugh, classic. was that introduced in the recent auth refactor?

maria: not sure. i grepped the sample: 
```
# example from docs
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("Redwood_API_KEY"))
```

maria: then they run `python sample.py` and get auth error. on mac/linux env var names are case-sensitive depending on shell/CI.

sam: thanks for filing. another related UX gotcha: the async sample uses `client.generate(..., retry=True)` but the sample shows synchronous usage in the README, so retries don't hook up in our async wrapper. i've seen requests fail without retries for transient 503s.

lena: can you paste the async snippet? i can look quick.

sam: pasted: 
```
# async snippet in quickstart
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient()

async def main():
    res = await client.generate("hello world", retry=True)
    print(res.text)

asyncio.run(main())
```

sam: problem is the sample never awaits client.__aenter__ or uses `async with RedwoodClient()` so internal retry/backoff loop for the async transport isn't initialized properly. it works fine if you do `async with RedwoodClient() as client:` or call `await client.connect()` first.

devon: OK — two fixes: docs change to use correct env var name and update async sample to use `async with` pattern. i'll draft a tiny PR.

maria: also can we add a short note about env var case-sensitivity for Windows users? windows env vars are case-insensitive but many CI systems and docker images aren't.

aaron: created GH issue <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/4682> summarizing both points (env var naming + async retry sample). i'll include repro and failing logs.

devon: cool. i'll open a docs PR referencing #4682 and rename the example to `os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")` and replace the async snippet with:
```
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def main():
    async with RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")) as client:
        res = await client.generate("hello world", retry=True)
        print(res.text)

asyncio.run(main())
```

lena: small nit: add a comment about closing the client/cleanup; otherwise people forget in longer-lived apps.

devon: yup will add that.

docs-bot: new PR opened: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5123> — changeset updates quickstart, adds env var note, and fixes async retry example. CI running. :github:

maria: amazing, thanks. can we also update the quickstart checksum in the snippets validation job so future drift is caught? the snippet linter didn't catch the env var mismatch because it's free-form text.

aaron: good idea — i'll add a tiny test in `tools/snippet-lint` to assert the example uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY` literal. i'll link the test in the PR.

sam: once PR lands, can we backport to the v1.x docs branch? a lot of enterprise customers still reference it.

devon: yes i'll open the backport after merge.

maria: closing loop — will retest onboarding flow tomorrow with intern. thanks all :thumbsup:
